title: Mailing One Letter Without Buying a Stamp Book
description: You can buy a single stamp for $1.44, or skip stamps with an online print-and-mail service. What each costs for a one-off letter, and what you still need.
answer: You do not have to buy a stamp book. Canada Post sells single stamps at $1.44 for a standard letter, against $1.24 each in a booklet. Or an online service prints, stamps and mails the letter for you, from $3.49 all in. Which is better depends on whether you have a printer and envelope.

blocks.p: A single stamp for a standard letter up to 30 g is $1.44. You still need the letter printed, an envelope, and a mailbox or post office. The [full cost comparison](/blog/what-it-costs-to-mail-a-letter-in-canada) adds the envelope and printing.

A print-and-mail service takes your document and addresses, prints it, folds it into a window envelope, applies the stamps and mails it. The cheapest sendletter letter is $3.49 with postage and tax included; [the breakdown](/blog/what-an-online-letter-costs) explains how it is built.

rows: Printer, envelope and a mailbox on your route
No printer, or no time for the errand
An online service: the letter is stamped and posted inside Canada
A booklet of stamps, or a service if the time saved is worth the difference

blocks.note: If you already have the printer, envelope and stamp, mailing it yourself is cheaper. A service earns its price when one of those is missing.
